name: Turkish Get-Up

beats.label: Floor
beats.cue: Keep one knee bent; bell above shoulder.

beats.label: Elbow
beats.cue: Rest on your free elbow and forearm.

beats.label: Bridge
beats.cue: Support hips on your hand and foot.

beats.label: Kneel
beats.cue: Front foot flat; rear knee down.

beats.label: Stand
beats.cue: Stand tall; reverse each step down.

setup: Start on your back with one kettlebell pressed above its shoulder.
Bend the knee on the bell side; extend the opposite leg.
Move through elbow, hand, bridge and kneeling before standing. Reverse each checkpoint to return, then repeat on the opposite side.

advice.tip: Keep the bell controlled above its shoulder; pause at each support change.
commonMistakes: Bending the loaded elbow or losing control of the bell.
Rushing the hand, foot or knee transfers.
Skipping the controlled return to the floor.

findings: Six connected whole-source checkpoints depict one side of the Turkish get-up. The player must reverse through kneel, bridge, hand and elbow before returning to floor; standing-to-floor reset is not a valid loop.

New whole-pose elbow-supported source has the free elbow and forearm resting on the floor, replacing the earlier fist-supported roll. This entire1512x1040 source is uniformly framed to756x520; this is whole-image framing, not an inverse preview-zoom claim or a fitted limb. The other five are native panel crops and integer translations.

Corrected half kneel faces right after the bridge, with front working foot planted and opposite knee down. Standing uses the original sheet's mild frontal view; the projected camera/body turn is a qualitative finding, not a fixed-camera certificate.

Canonical FA56 was attached to the joint sheet and each pose correction. The lean faceless white-grey athlete, featureless pelvis without shorts, fine contours and white trainers are reviewed qualitatively. Exact3D identity and segment measurements remain unverified.

Source-colour anatomical fields use the existing grey tone and contours: abs/front deltoids#7B72E9, obliques/glutes#9590E0. Chest is neutralised. Contour-following seeded palette regions are saved/reproducible; boundaries remain qualitative and some shoulder fields are occluded.
One grey kettlebell remains in the same working-side closed hand. Source-painted contact shadows and floor depth are illustrative; no recovered3D physical-contact or load-scale certificate.
The six images are held checkpoints, not continuously interpolated anatomy. Unshown transfer motion is explained in preparation/cues; opposite-side repetition is stated explicitly.
